newsitem.title: DENMARK: Copenhagen Airport reopens, fog still causes delays.
newsitem.headline: Copenhagen Airport reopens, fog still causes delays.

text.p: Copenhagen International Airport reopened on Thursday afternoon after being closed most of the morning due to heavy fog and landing system problems, but flights were still subject to major delays, airport and airline officials said.

"The landing system is working again and the airport is functioning but flow restrictions are in force due to the heavy fog, causing delays of up to two hours on flights," a SAS (Scandinavian Airlines System) spokesman told Reuters.
Over 60 percent of air traffic at Copenhagen, Europe's 11th biggest airport measured by traffic volume, is operated by SAS.

A Copenhagen International Airport Authority official said technical problems with the instrument landing system, which prevented incoming planes from landing for about 30 minutes during the morning, had been solved but confirmed that flights were subject to "relatively big delays."
During the morning incoming planes were diverted to either Stockholm, Sweden or Billund airport in west Denmark, he said.

He said delays in flight arrivals and departures would continue as long as the heavy fog persisted, adding that there was no immediate sign of the weather clearing up. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
